page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a memory-dense compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is configured at 168.0 GB, yielding an extensive memory density of 42.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a pronounced contrast between single-threaded compute strength and multi-threaded scaling. With its 4.2 GHz clock rate, the instance achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench performance of 2,351.0, paired with strong single-threaded compression speeds of 34.8 GB/sec in gzip and 14.37 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain modest due to the 4 vCPU limit, shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4,441.07 and weak software compilation throughput. Measured memory bandwidth reaches 345.37 GB/sec for small cached blocks, tapering to 36.1 GB/sec for uncached large reads. Static web serving reaches 8.39 GB/sec, while Redis operations log an average 6.27 million set operations per second.

From a hardware and cost efficiency perspective, the FX8-4ms_v2 offers high qualitative value for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing costs that nonetheless require vast operational memory. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates reliance on remote volumes, presenting an I/O tradeoff for data-intensive storage pipelines. Workloads aligned with this resource balance include memory-intensive relational database engines, Redis and in-memory caches, and single-threaded data analytics tasks.

The instance features zero local storage disks and no graphics accelerators.
